Subject: Quick follow-up — region assurance for pilot

Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Legal and procurement reviewed the high-level DPA and had two quick asks before we can move the pilot contract to signature:

1) We need evidence that all production inference for Cardinal Health will be pinned to US regions (no outbound processing to EU/APAC) except for a documented emergency failover.
2) If an emergency failover is required, we need the maximum hold window (how long data may be processed outside the US) and an audit trail format we can ingest.

Could you send (or point us to) the artifacts your team can provide so we can feed them to our InfoSec reviewers? A single PDF and a CSV roster of subprocessors would be ideal.

Appreciate a turnaround this week — procurement is trying to get the PO request into our finance queue.

Best,

Cardinal Health

Samantha — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Karthik (security/compliance) and Laura (legal ops) to attach the right artifacts. High-level answers here so you have context while we assemble documents: 

- Production inference for paid customer workloads can be pinned to US regions. Our platform supports strict region affinity; we persist customer model state and KV caches in the specified region.

- Temporary failover: our standard emergency failover window is up to 96 hours in the case of catastrophic region-wide outages. During that window data may route to an adjacent region for continuity (US-east <-> US-central). Cross-border (US->EU/APAC) processing only occurs under explicit customer opt-in or if a mutual legal hold requires transfer; we do not route US customer inference to EU/APAC for normal failover.

- Evidence: we will provide a single PDF that contains:
  * architecture diagram of regional tenancy and control plane separation
  * KMS key location and HSM boundary descriptions
  * audit log sample showing a pin-enforced request route
  * failover runbook excerpt with timelines and notification hooks

- Subprocessors: we maintain an up-to-date roster CSV that lists cloud infra providers, CDN partners, and observability tooling with processing locations.

I will have an assembled package by EOD tomorrow and will include the audit sample and HSM/KMS statement. Laura, Karthik — can you confirm the 96-hour wording and whether we can provide the sample audit in syslog-compatible format (CSV) that Cardinal can ingest?

Thanks,
Jonas
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Samantha, Jonas — attaching the artifacts requested. See the package contents below and quick notes on ingest formats.

Package (attached):
- residency_evidence_v1.pdf (PDF) — has diagrams, KMS/HSM statements, policy excerpts, and the failover runbook.
- subprocessor_roster_aug2027.csv (CSV) — canonical roster with location columns for each processor.
- audit_sample_us_pin.csv (CSV) — anonymized ingestion-friendly audit rows showing request timestamp, region, model_id, route_enforced_flag.

Quick notes:
- Failover: we can shorten the window by agreement (e.g., 24h or 48h) in the DPA addendum if Cardinal requires a stricter SLA. The 96-hour default is to cover multi-stage recovery (network, capacity, and verification).
- Audit format: audit_sample_us_pin.csv uses RFC3339 timestamps and a column (route_enforced=true/false) — should be straightforward to map into most SIEMs. We can also export JSON Lines on request.
- KMS: Customer keys can be BYOK (bring-your-own-key) via our KMS integration — keys remain in the US region of your choosing and are not exported. We note the HSM provider and key residency in the PDF.

Let me know if you need the audit rows in JSONL or compressed. Happy to stand up a short call to walk through the artifacts.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

1) InfoSec: The audit_sample_us_pin.csv looks good; can you add a column for "processing_duration_seconds" and include a sample row for an emergency failover event so we can validate our alert rules?
2) Procurement: we will accept a 48-hour hard limit in the DPA addendum (instead of the default 96h) if Redwood will commit to an operational escalation path that includes: 15-minute page to on-call, hourly status updates during failover, and a post-incident evidentiary bundle within 5 business days.

Are these items acceptable? If yes, we can proceed to final DPA redline and PO.

If helpful, we can set a 30-minute call tomorrow to confirm finer details.

Thanks,
